messages.text:
Let's try the following:

- pixels barrel: material after sensitive
- anywhere else: material before
- general rule: 1 mapping surface per sensitive layer
- additional mapping surfaces:
  - beampipe + inner/outer cylinders of pix-short strip, short - long strip gaps 
  - two discs between barrel and endcaps for all sub detectors
  -  outer detector shells



This should give us approximate 50 material surfaces.



- Charge the SoftEng to allow the definition of ProtoSurfaceMaterial on those portals
- Make only 1 bin in phi for the moment
  - bins in z for the barrel
    - 250 pixel & short strip, 100 long strip
    - 500 full gap cylinders, beam pipe 
  - bins r in the endcap (ec)
    - 50 pixel ec, and barrel-ec disk
    - 100 short strip ec, and barrel-ec disk
    - 50 long strip ec, and barrel-ec disk
    - 250 full shell disks



Make these numbers configurable:

- learn how to run the (nodd\_)material_mapping.py and (nodd\_)material_valdiation.py
- use the stacked material plot and overlay the validate one (no need for splitting into sub detectors, keep only put the total on top of the stacked one)

I’ll turn this into a configurable portal selection and binning scheme, assign SoftEng the native `ProtoSurfaceMaterial` support, then run mapping and validation and overlay the validated total on the stacked Geant4 profile. I’ll check the actual surface count against your approximate target of 50.

The native geometry has 52 sensitive layers before adding gap and shell surfaces, so these rules will likely produce about 65 unique physical surfaces. I’ll preserve one surface per layer and deduplicate shared portals. I’ll also use 500 z bins for the full outer shell cylinder, with that default configurable.

I’m continuing with the nODD coordination workflow and `acts-spack`. Preflight still reports changed environment fingerprints and no staged DD4hep/Geant4 sources; I’ll verify the installed runtime directly before using it.

SoftEng is assigned to the portal-material support and mapping/validation scripts. I’ll build the selection manifest and profile comparison.

For this trial, the full Geant4 recording—including silicon and beam pipe—will be mapped onto the selected portals. The mapping and validation geometry will clear its existing material slabs first, to avoid counting them twice.

The selection gives **65 unique portals: 15 cylinders and 50 discs**. One is shared: the outer pixel-barrel portal is also the inner pixel–short-strip gap cylinder. Its two roles request 250 and 500 z bins; I’ve made the conflict policy configurable and set this shared full cylinder to 500. The manifest records both requests.

SoftEng also confirmed that ACTS reads the saved pre-step positions directly, so it will add a local midpoint correction before mapping.

The portal support has compiled. Its smoke test found that the existing ACTS bindings and the current dependency view use different pybind11 ABIs. SoftEng is looking for matching installed headers; this does not require changing shared dependencies. The surface-selection checks and total-overlay code are ready.

The native smoke run now maps onto exactly 65 portals and reloads the saved map with all keys and binning intact. The full 100,000-track mapping run is next. After validation, I’ll overlay only the ACTS total on the original Geant4 stack, as requested.

The full run mapped all 17.1 million recorded steps onto 65 portals. Validation with 100,000 new rays is complete; its mean material totals are 0.51% higher in radiation lengths and 0.28% higher in interaction lengths. I’m now checking the profile shapes and preparing the overlays for review.

The η profiles differ by at most 1.10% in X₀ and 0.83% in λI across the retained bins. The φ comparison shows the cost of using one φ bin: differences reach about 85% in X₀ where the Geant4 material varies strongly with azimuth. I’ll retain that plot alongside the η overlays so the approximation is visible.

The overlays are rendered, and the saved map reloads with all 65 portal IDs and their requested bins intact. I’m finishing the source and evidence checks before an independent PhysVal review. The prototype still uses ACTS’s nearest-intersection assignment; “before” and “after” select the carrier’s side relative to the sensitive layer.

The implementation is ready for independent PhysVal review. It also passed a 1×1 binning smoke test, so the bin counts remain configurable down to one bin. I’m updating the PR’s discussion and token records while the reviewer checks the scientific interpretation.

The token records now include the completed SoftEng work and the finalized parent turn from the earlier survey. They exclude this still-active parent turn and the pending reviewer turn. The interaction ledger and token-site build pass with those accounting boundaries.
The GitHub connector cannot update PR metadata with its current permissions. I’m using the repository CLI to update the existing PR’s title and description.

PR #100’s description now covers the mapping and validation results. It links the bin configuration, native build guide, compressed map and validation overlays, while preserving the earlier material scatter and remote-material flags. PhysVal is checking the committed evidence independently.

PhysVal found no blocking defect in conservation, binning or profile normalization. It did quantify a substantial locality limitation: 56.6% of X₀ is assigned more than 50 mm from its recorded midpoint. I’m adding those diagnostics to the report and clarifying that validation generation settings are controlled by CLI flags; the JSON validation block records the intended run.

The report now includes the locality diagnostics, and the configuration wording is corrected. The independent checks reproduced every validation material-bin lookup and every recorded ray’s budget partition. I’m pushing the PR update and running the final repository checks.
